newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan Q&A, PART IV - Capacity utilization.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan Q&A, PART IV - Capacity utilization.

text.p: The following are excerpts from the question-and-answer session following the first leg of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins address before Congress.
Greenspan addressed the Senate Banking Committee at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.

SEN. MACK (R-FL) continued: "Today ... the ability to move production from one country to another seems to be prevalent. Therefore, it really raises again the question of the importance of capacity utilization, and I would make the argument in a number of other areas as well. I would be interested in your reaction to that."

GREENSPAN: "I think those arguments are valid with respect to long-term growth. There is no doubt that the extraordinary expansion of information technologies, computer applications of all sorts (and) the changing infrastructure of many markets as we deregulate them; that the underlying forces leading to higher growth may well be there and I certainly hope that is in fact the case.

"The business cycle, however, is a different breed. It occurs, apparently, as a conequence of human nature ... and therefore, what we tend to see from history, is significant variations of long-term trends in productivity enhancement in economic growth. But superimposed on that, a cyclical pattern of activity, which is to a certain extent, endogenous in that people's attitudes tend to overextend -- at least history has ... a degree of optimism building into various different types of over expansion which gluts markets and creates contractions. The most recent most obvious example is what happened to the commercial real estate industry, and that was really a big issue."
